title: Kirby's quiet leadership; Moore's return to the Victoria and Edgar Hayes
summary: Kirby was quiet while sidemen ran the band; after leaving he went back to the Victoria, then the Brickwood, with Edgar Hayes broadcasting from the Victoria.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it

blocks.x: So you left Kirby, and it was largely because the musicians started to get cranky, I guess, about the kind of back-up and so forth that they wanted, and Kirby didn't... Did he like your style? Or how did you get along with him as far as your style was concerned? Was it a
situation where what the band members wanted, and they sort of dictated...?
Well, John Kirby was all right to get along with. He didn't have very much to say.

Very quiet and didn't have much to say. But his band... The sidemen mostly ran that band. Syndicator(?). I would still say it's a syndicator(?). If they like you, they like you. If they don't like you, they don't like you. I did very good staying as long as I did, two years.

And after that band broke up, then I come on back up in Harlem at the Victoria. I stayed there about two years. Then they decided they wanted to start to broadcast from there. So we went out about three months... No, I'd say in about six months we went out, and went on down to the Brickwood. That's right across the street from where the Savoy used to be. The Brickwood was at 140th Street and Lenox Avenue. And this guy who had the band at his studio... I think he broadcast once a week from the Victoria. Sam...I can't think of his name, a piano player...he had the band... He wrote that number "Stardust." He didn't write it...
He had a five-piece band at the Victoria Cafe.
I see. So you joined his band.
We went out. We went back... No, then I went to the Brickwood.
When you say "we," it's you and who else?
Oh, the same band. Myself, Pete Brown and Donald Frye.
Oh, so in other words, that little trio stayed together.

You all left John Kirby, and what he did was replace everyone sort of altogether there. Okay. So you went back to the Victoria, and you stayed back at the Victoria for a little while, and you were one of two bands there, apparently, at the Victoria. Okay, I think that's...
So you were there for another couple of years, and then you were doing pretty much the same kinds of things. But do you remember the name of the gentleman who was broadcasting from the Victoria?
No, I don't remember who that was. All I remember was Edgar Hayes. He was the leader, he was the piano player...
